description: Creates a calendar of one tournament, by its league's code and its slug, and answers with its links: ncaamb and players-era-2026 for the Players Era, nba and emirates-nba-cup-2026 for the Emirates NBA Cup, fwwc and brazil-2027 for the FIFA Women's World Cup™ 2027. get_league_bracket answers a league's tournament with its slug. The calendar holds the tournament's games only, not the rest of its teams' seasons: every group game, and each knockout game once its two teams are known, so it fills in as the tournament is played. Its feed is the .ics address a calendar app subscribes to, and it stays up to date. Fails for a tournament we don't have.

league.description: The tournament's league's code, in any case: ncaamb.

tournament.description: The tournament's page segment under its league: players-era-2026.

name: create_tournament_calendar

subscribe.description: The whole addresses a person subscribes with, one for each calendar app, and what an assistant tells them.

appleUrl.description: The one-click link for Apple Calendar, on a Mac, iPhone or iPad: the feed's webcal address.

directions.description: What each link is for and why clicking one is safe, for an assistant to pass on to the person.

feedUrl.description: The feed's whole https address, for any other calendar app's "subscribe by URL".

googleUrl.description: The one-click link for Google Calendar. It opens Google Calendar with the feed ready to add, and the person confirms there. The only way into Google Calendar: Google offers an app no way to subscribe someone to a feed.

manageUrl.description: The page where the person changes the calendar's teams and settings later.

outlookUrl.description: The one-click link for Outlook on the web.

title: Create a calendar of a tournament
